card.title: SUPPLY TRAIN
card.text: Rail transport was the backbone of military logistics in WWII.
card.flavorText: Rail transport was essential to military logistics in WWII. All major powers used supply trains to move troops, weapons, fuel, food, and ammunition across vast distances. Germany’s blitzkrieg tactics relied on rail to sustain fast-moving forces. The Soviet Union used its network to shift armies and entire factories across thousands of kilometers. In the US, a vast rail system transported men and materiel from training bases to ports for overseas deployment. Trains delivered vital supplies to front-line units and were frequent targets for bombing and sabotage. Terrain, weather, and enemy action often disrupted operations, so armies built temporary tracks, used camouflage, and deployed mobile repair crews. Rail hubs became critical points of strategy, and some supply lines moved thousands of tons daily. In many campaigns, success depended on keeping the trains running.
